questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Farmer's Knowledge' refers to.
questions.a: Indian farming rests on knowledge handed down for millennia; the Krishi Parashara verse quoted in the chapter praises the farmer who knows his cattle, his seasons and his seeds, and is rewarded with harvests of every kind.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Farmer's Knowledge'.
questions.a: Farming is a science of observation: seasons, seeds and soil read carefully, season after season.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Farmer's Knowledge' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'How Farming Began' refers to.
questions.a: Farming began when communities learnt to save seeds and settle near fields: wild grasses were tamed into crops, forests cleared, and wandering food-gatherers slowly became villagers tied to the rhythm of sowing and harvest.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'How Farming Began'.
questions.a: The seed saved today is the field of tomorrow: settling down to grow food changed society forever.

questions.q: Under which section is 'How Farming Began' taught, and from which source text?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Crops of India' refers to.
questions.a: Indian fields grow a rich variety: rice in the monsoon wet, wheat and mustard in the winter cool, millets on dry land, besides cotton, sugarcane, tea and spices, each crop matched to its season and region.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Crops of India'.
questions.a: Crop follows climate: the same subcontinent grows rice in one state and wheat in another.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Crops of India' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Water for the Fields' refers to.
questions.a: Rain alone cannot feed the fields, so farmers built wells, tanks, canals and check dams from ancient times; irrigation lets a second crop grow and shields the harvest when the monsoon fails.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Water for the Fields'.
questions.a: Water is farming's first input: whoever stores and shares it wisely doubles the land's gift.
